name: python-acceptance
body: Acceptance for the Python frontend: fixtures scan cleanly on a scratch /tmp repo per no-real-project-test — a package fixture (a package with a sub-package), a flat-module fixture (distinct-stem files with no __init__.py in separate directories, e.g. `a/foo.py` and `b/bar.py`; it must NOT contain two same-stem flat modules, which alias and shadow under the documented limitation, python-package-identity), a cross-file call + base-class fixture, an unresolved-import fixture (third-party/vendored/dynamic), a code-type fixture (*_test.py, .pyi, a third_party/ path for external), and a site-packages exclusion fixture (a site-packages tree yields NO code nodes — it is a discovery exclusion, domain.constraint.python-exclusions, not a classified tree); a mixed-language repo scans py alongside another frontend into one graph without FQN collision. Tests assert the node/edge shapes and the unresolved categories. AC: the listed fixtures scan and the emitted nodes/edges match python-resolve-calls-uses, python-exactness-unresolved, python-package-identity and python-code-type (a third_party/ file classifies external; the site-packages fixture emits no node); the package-qualified and distinct-stem flat fixtures render the expected `py.<dotted-identity>` / `py.<stem>` FQNs with no two modules in the fixture set rendering to the same FQN, and the mixed-language fixture reports zero shadowed modules — no module is silently shadowed or merged away (src/ingest.rs:647-670) — and no same-kind symbol collision panics (`claim`, src/ingest.rs:88-96). The fixture set deliberately excludes two same-stem init-less modules in different directories, the aliasing limitation documented in python-package-identity.
